learning_objective: 🎯 You will learn the art of reporting what someone else said, both by quoting them exactly and by telling the story in your own words!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Direct speech is when you write the exact, real words that someone spoke. We always put their words inside special marks called quotation marks. For example: Rahul said, 'I am very hungry.'

Indirect speech (also called reported speech) is when you tell someone what another person said, but without using their exact words. We drop the quotation marks! For example: Rahul said that he was very hungry.
When you change direct speech to indirect speech, you usually take a step back in time because the words were spoken in the past! So, 'am' changes to 'was', and 'play' changes to 'played'.
In indirect speech, we also have to change pronouns so the sentence makes sense. If a girl says 'I like my dress', when you report it, you say 'She said that she liked her dress.'

fun_activity.title: ✍️ The Secret Reporter
fun_activity.instructions: Listen to a sentence your parent or sibling says. Write it down exactly with quotation marks (Direct), and then write it again reporting it as a secret message without quotes (Indirect)!

quick_recap: ⭐ Direct speech gives the exact words spoken and uses quotation marks.
⭐ Indirect speech reports what was said without using exact words or quotes.
⭐ When changing to indirect speech, present tenses usually change to past tenses.
⭐ Pronouns must also change to fit the perspective of the person reporting the speech.
